newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end up 1/8 point.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end up 1/8 point.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds ended Monday's somnolent session 1/8 point higher.

"We're just in a situation where there's not a lot of bonds around," one trader said. "There's not a lot of supply, so munis continue to grind a little bit higher like they have been doing for the past few weeks, and I don't see anything changing in the picture this week."

While the market receives key data this week including Tuesday's April figures on retail sales, Wednesday's producer price index and Thursday's consumer price index, the trader cited no overwhelming concern.
"I think there is some concern, but I think that people are generally expecting the numbers to be some what benign," he said.
Economists polled by Reuters expect a 0.3 percent decline in retail sales overall, and a 0.1 percent rise excluding autos.

Producer prices are expected to come in unchanged overall, with a 0.1 percent increase in the core rate, which excludes food and energy prices. CPI is expect to rise 0.1 overall, with a 0.2 percent rise predicted for the core rate.
But even if economic news is unfriendly, thin supply should help protect the market, the trader said.
"There's not going to be a lot of bonds around in the market, so it should be somewhat manageable," he said.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was up 2/32 at 96-22/32 to yield 6.89 percent in late trade in New York.
In debt futures, the June municipal bond contract closed up 16/32 at 115-25/32. The June T-bond contract closed up 13/32 at 110-7/32. The MOB spread was 178 ticks.
In muni cash, a municipal analyst said dollar bonds opened flat, rose 1/8 to 1/4 by noon, and then gave up 1/8 to finish 1/8 point higher.
High-grade issues ended flat to slightly higher.
Tuesday's new offerings are expected to total $840 million in 40 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $385 million in eight sales, with a $198 million Ocean County Utility Authority, N.J. deal through Dillion, Reed & Co., Inc. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 32 sales totaling $455 million are cheduled. A $139 million Cleveland City School District, Ohio, deal at 1100 EDT is the largest.
An additional five sales totaling $258 million are on the possible calender, meaning underwriters have said they may price the bonds Tuesday depending on market conditions.
